Fibrinolytic therapy.recommendation: When fibrinolysis is the reperfusion strategy, initiate treatment as soon as possible after diagnosis in the pre-hospital setting (aim for target of <10 min to lytic bolus).
Fibrinolytic therapy.notes: Emphasis on very early initiation; pre-hospital administration recommended.

Fibrinolytic therapy.recommendation: A fibrin-specific agent (i.e., tenecteplase, alteplase, or reteplase) is recommended.
A half-dose of tenecteplase should be considered in patients >75 years of age.
Fibrinolytic therapy.notes: Dose adjustment for older patients (>75 years).

Antiplatelet co-therapy with fibrinolysi.notes: Dual antiplatelet therapy recommended alongside fibrinolysis.

Anticoagulation co-therapy with fibrinol.recommendation: Anticoagulation is recommended in patients treated with fibrinolysis until revascularization (if performed) or for the duration of hospital stay (up to 8 days).
Anticoagulation co-therapy with fibrinol.notes: Use anticoagulation during acute management post-fibrinolysis.

Anticoagulation co-therapy with fibrinol.recommendation: Enoxaparin i.v. followed by s.c. is recommended as the preferred anticoagulant.
Anticoagulation co-therapy with fibrinol.notes: Specifies enoxaparin (intravenous then subcutaneous) as preferred.

Anticoagulation co-therapy with fibrinol.recommendation: When enoxaparin is not available, unfractionated heparin (UFH) is recommended as a weight-adjusted i.v. bolus followed by infusion.
Anticoagulation co-therapy with fibrinol.notes: UFH as alternative when enoxaparin unavailable; weight-adjusted dosing.

Anticoagulation co-therapy with fibrinol.recommendation: In patients treated with streptokinase, an i.v. bolus of fondaparinux followed by an s.c. dose 24 h later should be considered.
